questions.question: Build the appropriation account of Molefe and de Waal Traders from a net profit of R421 000 and prove that the whole profit is distributed.
questions.expected_answer: Net profit of R421 000 enters on the credit side of the appropriation account. The agreement is executed in order: interest on capital at 9 percent — R36 000 to Molefe and R27 000 to de Waal, R63 000 together; partners' salaries — R120 000 to Molefe and R144 000 to de Waal, R264 000 together; and a bonus of R10 000 to de Waal for meeting the sales target. That appropriates R337 000, leaving R84 000, shared four to three: R48 000 to Molefe and R36 000 to de Waal. Proof: Molefe receives R36 000 plus R120 000 plus R48 000 — R204 000; de Waal receives R27 000 plus R144 000 plus R10 000 plus R36 000 — R217 000; and R204 000 plus R217 000 equals R421 000, so the account balances and the whole profit is distributed. Partners' salaries and interest on capital are appropriations of profit, never expenses, so they do not reduce net profit.

questions.question: Write up both partners' current accounts for the year, including de Waal's opening debit balance, and interpret each closing balance.
questions.expected_answer: Molefe's current account: credit side — balance brought down R8 200, interest on capital R36 000, salary R120 000, share of remaining profit R48 000, totalling R212 200; debit side — drawings R176 000; closing balance R36 200 credit, meaning the business owes Molefe R36 200. De Waal's current account opens with R5 400 on the debit side because last year he drew more than he earned. Credit side — interest on capital R27 000, salary R144 000, bonus R10 000, profit share R36 000, totalling R217 000; debit side — the opening R5 400 plus drawings of R182 000, totalling R187 400; closing balance R29 600 credit, meaning he has worked out of the debit and the business now owes him R29 600. Capital contributions never appear here — they belong in the fixed capital accounts. Together the current accounts hold R65 800 of undrawn earnings that joins capital in equity.

questions.question: Analyse these events on the accounting equation: de Waal contributes R50 000 by EFT; Molefe takes stock of R3 000 for personal use; interest on capital of R36 000 is allowed to Molefe; interest of R18 000 is capitalised on the loan; a creditor is paid R14 000.
questions.expected_answer: The method is to write the double entry, classify each account, then read the effects. Capital contribution: debit Bank, credit Capital — assets up R50 000, equity up R50 000, liabilities nil. Stock taken: debit Drawings, credit Trading stock at cost — assets down R3 000, equity down R3 000, liabilities nil. Interest on capital allowed: debit Appropriation, credit Current account of Molefe — both equity accounts, so total equity is unchanged; the allowance redistributes equity from the profit pool to Molefe's claim, with no effect on assets or liabilities. Capitalised interest: debit Interest on loan, credit Loan — equity down R18 000, liabilities up R18 000, assets untouched. Paying the creditor: debit Creditors control, credit Bank — assets down R14 000, liabilities down R14 000, equity untouched, because settling a debt is not an expense. In every case the equation stays level, which is the built-in check.
